newsitem.title: TAIWAN: HK rejects visa for popular Taiwan ex-minister.
newsitem.headline: HK rejects visa for popular Taiwan ex-minister.

text.p: One of Taiwan's most popular politicians said on Monday he was denied a permit to enter Hong Kong to witness its handover to Beijing, a decision he condemned as "ridiculous".
"I don't have a clue why my visa was rejected," former justice minister Ma Ying-jeou told Reuters.
"They wanted me to postpone my visit. In other words, they wanted to avoid the politically sensitive time of the handover," Ma said in a telephone interview.
Taiwan's exiled Republic of China will be represented at the handover by Koo Chen-fu, head of the semi-official Straits Exchange Foundation that handles informal ties with Beijing.
China regards Taiwan as a renegade province and threatens to retake the island by force if it declares independence.

Ma, who rocked the ruling Nationalist Party when he quit the cabinet in May, found it odd that Hong Kong had admitted him in January when he was a minister without portfolio but now was rejecting him as an ordinary citizen.
"It is very ridiculous. How come my visit to Hong Kong becomes more difficult when Hong Kong is about to revert to mainland Chinese rule?" said Ma, who was born in Hong Kong.
"Why is my status as private citizen sensitive? Rejecting a Hong Kong-born person's return to Hong Kong to watch the handover is extremely unreasonable."

Ma was the Nationalists' best hope for winning the Taipei mayoralty back from the opposition Democratic Progressive Party until he removed himself from the political arena in May, saying he wanted to pursue an academic career.
